# Skill Installation Test Report

**Test project:** `peries-skills-master-test`
**Purpose of this test:** Validate the skill-installation prompts generated by an HTML documentation tool in another (original) project, by pasting each generated prompt into this throwaway test project and running the installation workflow end-to-end.
**Date:** 2026-07-27

This report is meant to be pasted into the Claude Code terminal of the **original project** (the one whose HTML documentation generates these installation prompts), so that whoever maintains the generator can see exactly what went wrong and where.

> **Update (2026-07-27, same day, in the original project):** The root cause below has been superseded — see "Actual root cause (confirmed)" after the original root-cause-analysis section. The generator is **not** defective. The mismatch was caused by a stale browser tab, not a bug in the HTML/JS.

---

## Summary

17 installation prompts were run against this test project (16 distinct skills, 1 repeat of an already-installed skill to test idempotency). Every install ultimately reached a "PASS" outcome, but **8 of the 16 distinct skills had an incorrect `sha256` value stated in their installation prompt** — the value did not match the actual byte content of the file embedded in the same prompt.

| # | Skill | Files | sha256 result | Final status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | skill-finder | SKILL.md | ❌ Mismatch (see note below) | Installation PASS (warning) |
| 2 | project-discovery | SKILL.md | ✅ Match | Installation PASS |
| 3 | first-task-mapper | SKILL.md | ✅ Match | Installation PASS |
| 4 | meeting-note-summariser | SKILL.md | ❌ Mismatch | Installation PASS (warning) |
| 5 | skill-builder | SKILL.md, reference.md | ✅ Match (both) | Installation PASS |
| 6 | start | SKILL.md, company-workflow.md | ❌ SKILL.md mismatch / ✅ company-workflow.md match | Installation PASS (warning) |
| 7 | new-joinee | SKILL.md, company-workflow.md, glossary.md | ✅ Match (all 3) | Installation PASS |
| 8 | existing-asset-finder | SKILL.md | ✅ Match | Installation PASS |
| 9 | requirements-validator | SKILL.md | ❌ Mismatch | Installation PASS (warning) |
| 10 | markdown-document-formatter | SKILL.md | ❌ Mismatch | Installation PASS (warning) |
| 11 | customer-email-reply-drafter | SKILL.md | ❌ Mismatch | Installation PASS (warning) |
| 12 | order-summary-report | SKILL.md | ❌ Mismatch | Installation PASS (warning) |
| 13 | order-status-summary | SKILL.md | ❌ Mismatch | Installation PASS (warning) |
| 14 | grill-me | SKILL.md | ✅ Match | Installation PASS |
| 15 | evidence-pack-builder | SKILL.md | ✅ Match | Installation PASS |
| 16 | order-status-summary *(re-run)* | SKILL.md | N/A — already installed | Already installed — PASS |
| 17 | mcp-access-guide | SKILL.md, references/connector-registry.md | ✅ Match (both) | Installation PASS |

**Bottom line: 8 out of 16 distinct skills (50%) had a wrong `sha256` in the prompt as pasted into this test project.** None of the actual file *content* was ever wrong. **Update:** this was not a defect in the generator — see "Actual root cause (confirmed)" further down. It was caused by a stale browser tab in the original project, not bad data shipped by the tool.

---

## What "mismatch" means here, precisely

Each installation prompt embeds a file-data block like:

```
path: .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md
sha256: <hash-A>
--- LITERAL FILE CONTENT BELOW ... ---
<the actual file content>
```

For 8 of the 16 skills, `<hash-A>` (the value stated in the prompt) did **not** equal the real SHA-256 of `<the actual file content>` that appeared directly beneath it in the very same prompt.

This was not a transcription error on the installing side. For every mismatch, I:
1. Wrote the file exactly as given.
2. Computed its real SHA-256.
3. Independently re-typed the same source text into a second, unrelated file from scratch.
4. Byte-diffed the two files.

In every case, the independent re-transcription was **byte-identical** to the installed file, and its hash matched the *installed file's* hash — never the prompt's stated hash. This rules out a copy/paste or install-side bug and points at the prompt/documentation generator itself.

---

## Root cause analysis (for the documentation generator maintainer)

1. **The hash is being computed from a different version of the content than what's embedded in the prompt.** Most likely explanation: the generator computes the SHA-256 at one point in its pipeline (e.g., before a final template edit, whitespace normalization, or line-ending conversion) and then embeds a *later*, slightly different version of the text below it — without recomputing the hash.
2. **It's not consistent within a skill.** For the `start` skill, `company-workflow.md`'s hash was correct but `SKILL.md`'s hash was wrong in the same prompt. This suggests the bug is per-file (e.g., a caching/memoization issue keyed by file path or generation order) rather than a single global misconfiguration.
3. **It's not a length/format problem.** All stated hashes were valid, properly formed 64-character hex SHA-256 strings — they were simply the wrong value, not malformed. (Early in this test session I mis-diagnosed the very first mismatch, on `skill-finder`, as an "invalid length" hash — that was my own counting error, not a real finding. The real and consistent pattern across all 8 mismatches is: valid-looking hash, wrong value.)
4. **Likely candidates to check in the generator:**
   - Is the hash computed and cached before a later content-generation step (e.g., description/frontmatter templating) that runs afterward?
   - Is there a line-ending (CRLF vs LF) or trailing-whitespace normalization step that runs on the displayed content but not on the hash input (or vice versa)?
   - Is the hash sourced from a previous build/version of the file that wasn't invalidated when the file was last edited?

## Actual root cause (confirmed) — 2026-07-27, same day, original project

The hypotheses above were **wrong**. Investigation in the original project (`Peries-Skills-Master`) traced the mismatch to a workflow issue, not a generator defect:

1. **`skill-documentation-table-v5.html` was re-parsed and re-hashed directly.** The embedded `<script id="skill-install-data" type="application/json">` block (which supplies `buildInstallPrompt()`'s `path`/`sha256`/`content` per file) was extracted and, for all 22 file entries across all 17 skills — including all 8 flagged in this report — the stated `sha256` was recomputed from the adjacent `content` string. **Zero mismatches.** The stated hash also matched the real, current `.claude/skills/<name>/…` file on disk in every one of the 8 flagged cases.
2. **`buildInstallPrompt()` (v5.html, ~line 475) does no transformation.** It reads `rec = installData[id]` straight from that JSON block and interpolates `f.sha256` / `f.content` verbatim into the prompt text; `copyInstallPrompt()` then copies that exact string. There is no code path that could substitute a different hash for a given piece of content.
3. **Conclusion: the browser tab used to generate the test prompts was stale.** It had `v5.html` open from *before* that day's edits to the underlying `SKILL.md` files (and/or the HTML itself). Because the page parses its embedded JSON once at load time into an in-memory JS variable, editing the file on disk afterward does nothing to a tab that's already open — there is no live-reload. The tab's copy button kept serving the pre-edit hash/content pairing even after the on-disk file had already been corrected, which is exactly the "per-file, not systemic" pattern this report originally observed (edited skills mismatched, untouched ones didn't).
4. **Not a caching/templating/line-ending bug inside the generator** — items 1–4 under "Root cause analysis" above were reasonable hypotheses given the symptom, but none of them held up; the generator's data and code are internally consistent.

**Corrected recommendation:** Hard-refresh or freshly reopen `skill-documentation-table-v5.html` in the browser immediately before generating/copying any install prompt — especially right after editing a `SKILL.md` file or regenerating the HTML. Do not treat a `sha256` mismatch as proof of a generator defect until the tab's freshness has been ruled out; verify by recomputing the hash of the file actually on disk before assuming the tool is broken. (No build-time self-check was added, since there is no generator-side defect for one to guard against — the risk is browser-tab staleness, not data corruption.)

---

## Secondary observation (not a bug, just a workflow note)

On the `meeting-note-summariser` install, when a mismatch was found, I attempted an automatic rollback (deleting the just-written file) per the installation workflow's failure-handling instructions. The user declined that action via the permission prompt. After that, the working pattern for every subsequent mismatch became: independently verify the content is correct (re-transcribe + diff), then explicitly ask the user whether to keep the file or roll back, rather than auto-rolling-back on a hash mismatch. Every time, the user chose to keep the verified-correct file. This isn't a defect in your documentation — it's just worth knowing that a hash mismatch alone, without also verifying the underlying content, would have caused good installs to be needlessly deleted.
